question: Bimal starts from Point Y and drives 44 km towards south. He then takes a left turn, drives 56 km, turns right and drives 37 km. He then takes a right turn and drives 23 km. He takes a right turn, drives 28 km. He then turns right, drives 38 km, turns left and drives 53 km, turns right and drives 19 km to stop at Point Z. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point Y again? (All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution:
• Bimal starts from Point Y and drives 44 km towards south.
 
• He then takes a left turn, drives 56 km, turns right and drives 37 km.
 
• He then takes a right turn and drives 23 km.
 
• He takes a right turn, drives 28 km.
 
• He then turns right, drives 38 km, turns left and drives 53 km, turns right and drives 19 km to stop at Point Z.
